questions.text: Which of the following territories does not belong to Great Britain?
questions.explanation: ‘Great Britain’ refers only to England, Scotland and Wales, not to Northern Ireland. The official name of the country is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

questions.text: Who was the first Briton to win the ‘Tour de France’?
questions.explanation: Bradley Wiggins became the first Briton to win the ‘Tour de France’.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.explanation: The English language has many accents and dialects.

options.text: The English language has no dialects
The English language has many accents and dialects
Gaelic is spoken in North Wales
In Northern Ireland people speak French

questions.text: How old do you need to be to go into betting shops or gambling clubs?
questions.explanation: In the UK, you have to be 18 to go into betting shops or gambling clubs.

questions.text: What do Ian McEwan, Hilary Mantel and Julian Barnes have in common?
questions.explanation: The Man Booker Prize for Fiction is awarded annually for the best fiction novel written by an author from the Commonwealth, Ireland or Zimbabwe. It has been awarded since 1968. Past winners include Ian McEwan, Hilary Mantel and Julian Barnes.

options.text: They were awarded with the Man Booker Prize for Fiction
They won a Nobel Prize in Literature
They were awarded with the Mercury Music Prize

questions.text: In Northern Ireland members of the Legislative Assembly are elected on the basis of:
questions.explanation: The Northern Ireland Assembly has 90 elected members, known as MLAs (members of the Legislative Assembly). They are elected with a form of proportional representation.

questions.text: How can MPs be contacted (choose TWO options)?
questions.explanation: You can contact MPs by letter or telephone at their constituency office, or at their office in the House of Commons: The House of Commons, Westminster, London SW1A OAA, telephone 0207729 3000.

options.text: By going to your local council and asking for an appointment

questions.text: What did the’Bill of Rights’ confirm in 1689?
questions.explanation: The Bill of Rights, 1689, confirmed the rights of Parliament and the limits of the king’s power. Parliament took control of who could be monarch and declared that the king or queen must be a Protestant.

options.text: The rights of Parliament and the limits of the king’s power
The supreme power of the king

questions.text: Who designed the Clifton Suspension Bridge located over the Avon George?
questions.explanation: The Clifton Suspension Bridge was designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel.

questions.text: Does Britain have a written constitution?
questions.explanation: The British constitution is not written down in any single document, and therefore it is described as ‘unwritten’. This is mainly because the UK, unlike America or France, has never had a revolution which led permanently to a totally new system of government.

questions.text: What was the estimated population of the British Empire during the Victorian period?
questions.explanation: During the Victorian period, the British Empire grew to cover all of India, Australia and large parts of Africa. It became the largest empire the world has ever seen, with an estimated population of more than 400 million people.

questions.text: Which of the following countries was NOT part of the Allied Powers during the First World War?
questions.explanation: Bulgaria formed part of the Central Powers during the First World War.

questions.text: How many times have the Olympic Games been hosted in the UK?
questions.explanation: The UK has hosted the Olympic games on three occasions: 1908, 1948 and 2012.

questions.text: When were films first shown publicly in the UK?
questions.explanation: Films were first shown publicly in the UK in 1896 and film screenings very quickly became popular.

questions.text: What is the name of the building where the Welsh government members meet?
questions.explanation: Elected members of the Welsh government meet at the Senedd in Cardiff, the capital city of Wales.

questions.text: Where is the city of Southampton located?
questions.explanation: Southampton is located in England.

questions.text: When did the First World War finish?
questions.explanation: The First World War ended at 11.00 am on 11th November 1918 with victory for Britain and its allies.

questions.text: Florence Nightingale was known for her work on:
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale is often regarded as the founder of modern nursing.

options.text: The development of nursing in the UK
The development and manufacture of motor-sport technology

questions.text: Which Act abolished slavery throughout the British Empire in 1833?
questions.explanation: In 1833 the Emancipation Act abolished slavery throughout the British Empire. The Royal Navy stopped slave ships from other countries, freed the slaves and punished the slave traders.

questions.text: How long does Diwali last for?
questions.explanation: Diwali normally falls in October or November and lasts for five days.

questions.text: Who became King of Britain when Queen Anne died in 1714?
questions.explanation: When Queen Anne died in 1714, Parliament chose a German, George I, to be the next king, because he was Anne’s nearest Protestant relative.

questions.text: What was the population of the UK in 2005?
questions.explanation: The population of the UK in 2005 was just under 60 million people.

questions.text: When did the ‘Habeas Corpus Act’ become law?
questions.explanation: The Habeas Corpus Act became law in 1679.

questions.text: Who discovered the penicillin in 1928?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming was researching influenza (the ‘flu’) in 1928 when he discovered penicillin.
